title: Observing the magic Mpemba effect in localized dynamics on a digital quantum computer
authors: Han-Ze Li, Xianquan Yan, Yi-Rui Zhang, Jian-Xin Zhong, Shuo Liu, Ching Hua Lee
abstract: The Mpemba effect challenges the intuition that states closer to equilibrium must relax faster. We ask whether an analogous magic-ordering reversal can occur in the generation of quantum magic (nonstabilizerness), a key resource for universal quantum computation: can a state with less initial magic overtake one with more and reach its asymptotic value sooner? Here, we uncover interaction-induced dephasing as a distinct mechanism for this magic Mpemba effect, requiring neither transport nor conventional thermalization. For tilted product states in an interacting $\ell$-bit model, a random-phase analysis predicts a reversal of the magic ordering: states with less initial magic attain higher saturated magic, independent of their spatial pattern. Exact simulations of the $\ell$-bit model and localized spin chains further show that these states also saturate earlier. We observe both features on IBM superconducting quantum processors. An effective $\ell$-bit implementation accesses long dephasing times at fixed circuit depth by encoding time in gate angles, while a microscopic spin model exhibits the reversal universally across initial patterns in the localized regime but only selectively in the ergodic regime. These results establish interaction-induced dephasing as a route to anomalous quantum-resource relaxation beyond transport-driven thermalizing dynamics.
summary: This paper explores a 'magic Mpemba effect' in quantum systems, showing that quantum resources like 'magic' can exhibit counter-intuitive relaxation dynamics. The effect is attributed to interaction-induced dephasing, a mechanism distinct from standard thermalization. The findings are supported by theoretical analysis, simulations across multiple models, and direct measurements on quantum hardware.
main_problem: The paper investigates an anomalous 'magic Mpemba effect' (MME) in quantum resource generation, specifically determining if a reversal in the rate of nonstabilizerness (magic) can occur without relying on conventional transport or thermalization mechanisms.
main_result: The MME was confirmed, showing that states with less initial quantum magic can reach a higher saturated magic value and saturate earlier than expected, attributing this to interaction-induced dephasing.
method: The study combines theoretical random-phase analysis with exact numerical simulations and direct measurements on superconducting quantum processors to quantify the resource dynamics.
model_or_system: The research utilizes several models, including the phenomenological $\ell$-bit model for Many-Body Localization (MBL) and microscopic spin chains (TFS, TNS, TDWS). Experiments are conducted on IBM superconducting quantum processors.
key_observables: Magic density ($M_2$), saturation time ($t_{ss}$), and level spacing statistics ($\langle r angle$).
important_parameters: Tilt angle ($	heta$), system size ($N$), and the distinction between localized vs. ergodic dynamical regimes.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the observed effect is due to interaction-induced dephasing, which is confirmed by the absence of the effect in the non-interacting (Anderson) limit.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the MME signatures ($M_2$ vs. time $t$) showing reversals, and also display level spacing statistics confirming the transition between ergodic (GOE) and localized (Poisson) regimes.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from theoretical modeling ($\ell$-bit model) to detailed simulation across various microscopic spin chains, culminating in experimental verification on superconducting hardware, while consistently contrasting the findings between localized and ergodic dynamics.
why_interesting: This work provides a novel mechanism (interaction-induced dephasing) for anomalous relaxation of quantum resources, extending the concept of the Mpemba effect beyond classical thermodynamics into the realm of quantum information theory.
